# Results — Study 93 (Round-Numbers) on the real tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Two tests, one basket
(^GSPC · SPY · AAPL · MSFT): **(a)** a chi-square that the distance from each close to its
nearest round level is uniform, and **(b)** a round-number **fade** as a fixed-horizon
event study — when the close sits within **0.4%** of a round level, bet on a reversal *away*
from it, enter one day later (signal at close *t* → entry at *t+1*), hold **1 day**, and
record the signed return **demeaned by the tape's own drift**. The fade is pinned against a
**random-level control** that fades the same grid spacing at a random phase (200 seeds).
As-of **2026-06-12**; match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## (a) Clustering — is the distance-to-round distribution non-uniform?

| Series | n | chi² (10 bins) | p | Within 5% of round |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ^GSPC | 9,179 | 16.9 | 5.0e-02 | 9.7% |
| SPY | 8,399 | 34.3 | 7.9e-05 | 9.6% |
| AAPL | 9,179 | 50.3 | 9.5e-08 | 10.3% |
| MSFT | 9,179 | 67.7 | 4.3e-11 | 9.8% |
| **POOLED (whole-dollar scale)** | **35,936** | **380.4** | **2.0e-76** | **11.2%** (uniform 10.0%) |

The clustering is **real and overwhelming** pooled (chi² = 380.4, p ≈ 2.0e-76; 11.2% of
closes land within 5% of a whole dollar vs the 10% a uniform distribution predicts), and it
clears the bar name-by-name for the single stocks (MSFT p = 4e-11, AAPL p = 1e-7). The
effect is strongest on individual names and faint on the index — exactly the Harris (1991)
shape. → Signal (clustering) **REAL**.

## (b) Tradability — does proximity to a round level forecast a reversal?

| Arm | Trades | Mean / trade | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| ^GSPC fade | 1,347 | +0.17 bps | +0.06 |
| SPY fade | 1,390 | −4.56 bps | −1.38 |
| AAPL fade | 1,066 | −8.62 bps | −0.89 |
| MSFT fade | 839 | +15.31 bps | +1.81 |
| **POOLED real fade (gross)** | **4,642** | **−0.53 bps** | **−0.18** |
| Pooled fade, net of 5 bps/leg | 4,642 | **−10.53 bps** | — |
| Random-level fade (200 seeds) | — | −0.10 bps (sd 2.77) | — |

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Does the fade forecast a reversal? | **No** — pooled mean **−0.53 bps/trade**, HAC *t* = **−0.18** |
| Does it beat a random-level fade? | **No** — it wins only **43% of 200 seeds** (a coin-flip, leaning *worse* than random) |
| Survives costs? | **No** — net of 5 bps/leg the gross −0.53 bps becomes **−10.53 bps/trade** |

## How to read it

- **The clustering is real.** Prices genuinely pile up near round numbers — pooled chi² of
  380.4 (p ≈ 2.0e-76) is not a fluke, and it is exactly what the price-discreteness
  literature has documented for sixty years. → Signal **REAL** on the *distribution*.
- **But proximity forecasts nothing.** The fade's next-day return is statistically
  indistinguishable from zero (−0.53 bps, HAC *t* = −0.18), and it does **not** beat a
  random-level fade (43% of seeds) — the round levels carry no information a trader can bank.
  → Signal **NONE** on the *forecast*; 3rd axis **"Beats a random level? → NOT SUPPORTED"**.
- **As a strategy it is a mirage.** Even gross it doesn't pay; charge a realistic 5 bps/leg
  and every fade bleeds ~10 bps. → Tradability **MIRAGE**.

A clustering fact dressed up as a trading signal: the magnetism is in the *ruler*, not the
*future*.

## Reproduce

```bash
python examples/verify.py             # real tape (this doc)
python examples/run_synthetic_demo.py  # offline positive/negative control
```
